record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures Associated with the Invariant Subspace Problem
record.original_question: Does every positive operator on a separable Banach lattice have a non-trivial closed invariant subspace, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} and M not equal to the whole Banach lattice such that the operator maps M into M?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable infinite-dimensional real Banach lattice (i.e., a real Banach space equipped with a partial order $\le$ compatible with the vector space operations such that $(X,\le)$ is a vector lattice, and whose norm is a lattice norm: $|x|\le|y|$ implies $\|x\|\le\|y\|$, where $|x|=x\vee(-x)$). A bounded linear operator $T:X\to X$ is called positive if $Tx\ge 0$ for every $x\ge 0$. A closed subspace $M\subseteq X$ is called a non-trivial closed invariant subspace for $T$ if $M\ne\{0\}$, $M\ne X$, and $T(M)\subseteq M$.

Question: Does every positive bounded linear operator on every separable infinite-dimensional Banach lattice have a non-trivial closed invariant subspace?
artifact.category_tag: Invariant subspaces of positive operators on Banach lattices
artifact.status_search_result: The invariant subspace problem for positive operators on separable Banach lattices remains open in general. Partial results exist (e.g., for positive strictly singular operators, for lattice homomorphisms on spaces with unconditional bases, and various commutant/domination conditions of Abramovich–Aliprantis–Burkinshaw type), but no complete affirmative or negative answer is known.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspaces for positive operators on Banach spaces with unconditional basis
status_evidence.snippet: Every lattice homomorphism acting on a Banach space with the lattice structure given by an unconditional basis has a non-trivial closed invariant subspace.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available; the general problem is still investigated.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspaces of positive strictly singular operators on Banach lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Every positive strictly singular operator on a Banach lattice satisfying certain conditions is AM-compact and has invariant subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Special subclasses of positive operators are known to have invariant subspaces, but the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspace problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The invariant subspace problem is a partially unresolved problem in functional analysis.
status_evidence.claim: The invariant subspace problem is broadly open, including for positive operators on separable Banach lattices in general.
